title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 740-741 of the sequel to La Longue Marche): Grothendieck asks whether the right setting for general Teichmüller groups is 'L-groups' rather than 'groupes à lacets'. An L-group is a group with a distinguished conjugacy class of (pro)cyclic 'loop' subgroups, here the cusp or parabolic subgroups, together with an orientation module. His model example is Γ^+_{0,3} ≅ PSL(2,Z) ≅ Z/3 * Z/2. In his indexing this is the orbifold fundamental group of the j-line, i.e. of M_{0,4}/S_3 (his 'M_{0,3}'). Its L-structure is the conjugacy class of the parabolic subgroup generated by (1 -1; 0 1), or by (1 0; 1 1).

On this page he finishes a sentence begun on p. 740. That page notes the 'remarkable property' of the discrete L-group: every direct L-automorphism (one acting trivially on the orientation module) is inner. Here he conjectures that this property characterizes Γ^+_{0,3} up to a non-unique isomorphism, when combined with one of two further conditions:
- trivial centre; or, better,
- every finite-index subgroup has trivial centralizer.

NB: to prove that every L-automorphism is inner, the key step is to show that it preserves Π_{0,3}. This is the kernel of 1 → Π_{0,3} → Γ^+_{0,3} → S_3 → 1. Π_{0,3} is free of rank 2, ≅ Γ(2)/±1 = π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}).

He states a stronger claim: every group automorphism, not only L-automorphisms, preserves Π_{0,3}. This follows from a lemma: if Π is normal with Γ^+_{0,3}/Π ≅ S_3, then Π = Π_{0,3}. More precisely, every surjection Γ^+_{0,3} → S_3 is conjugate to the canonical one.

Proof, begun here and completed on p. 741. Use the presentation ρ^3 = σ^2 = 1. If one generator dies, the image is cyclic of order at most 3. So an image of order ≥ 4 forces ρ to map to an element of order 3 and σ to one of order 2. In S_3 this means a 3-cycle (2 choices) and a transposition (3 choices), giving 6 surjections in all. These form a single orbit under Inn(S_3) = Aut(S_3) ≅ S_3, so all are conjugate.

The argument is correct and elementary. It makes Π_{0,3} characteristic in PSL(2,Z). Combined with Aut(PSL2(Z)) = PGL2(Z), this gives the inner-ness of direct automorphisms in the discrete case.
errors: No error in the lemma or its proof (discrete case; the same argument also works for the profinite completion, since torsion of order 2 and 3 survives and ρ, σ topologically generate).

Caveat on the conjectured characterization, if read profinitely, as the machine transcription's hats suggest. For the profinite completion of PSL(2,Z), not every 'direct' L-automorphism is inner. Elements of Gal(Q̄/Q) in the kernel of the cyclotomic character preserve the cusp inertia class and act trivially on the orientation module. By Belyi faithfulness on Π_{0,3}^ (which is characteristic by this very lemma), they give non-inner outer automorphisms. The same holds for GT elements with λ = 1.
The characterization conjecture itself is vague. The class of competing L-groups and the exact hypotheses are unspecified, so it is not checkable as stated.

ideas.what: Every surjection PSL(2,Z) = Z/3*Z/2 → S_3 is conjugate to the canonical one, so the kernel Γ(2)/±1 ≅ F_2 is characteristic (preserved by all automorphisms).
ideas.modern_name: Characteristic principal congruence subgroup Γ(2) in PSL(2,Z); counting epimorphisms from free products
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore / classical (follows from Aut PSL2(Z) = PGL2(Z), Hua–Reiner era)

ideas.what: L-groups (groups with a distinguished conjugacy class of cyclic 'loop' subgroups and an orientation module), and their 'Teichmüller group' defined as outer L-automorphisms.
ideas.modern_name: Groups with peripheral structure / 'groupes à lacets'; outer automorphisms preserving inertia (as in the GT and anabelian setting)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (groupes à lacets in Esquisse d'un programme); peripheral structures in 3-manifold topology (Waldhausen and others)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions 'groupes à lacets'; the L-group variant is unsure

ideas.what: Conjecture: PSL(2,Z) is characterized among L-groups by 'every direct L-automorphism is inner' together with trivial centre, or trivial centralizers of finite-index subgroups.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity / characterization by trivial (direct) outer automorphism group

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes that PSL(2,Z), as an L-group, is characterized up to isomorphism by having all direct L-automorphisms inner plus a centralizer condition. He leaves this unproved and imprecise.
missed.quote: Il se pourrait que cette propriété, ajoutée à celle que le centre est trivial (ou mieux, peut-être, que le centralisateur de tout sous-groupe d'indice fini est réduit à {1}) caractérise Γ^+_{0,3} à isomorphisme (non unique) près.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an intrinsic group-theoretic characterization of the modular group via its peripheral structure. If made precise, it would sit beside rigidity results for Fuchsian groups. Its profinite analogue visibly fails because of the Galois/GT actions, which is exactly where Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory lives.

missed.claim: The notion of a 'Teichmüller group of an L-group' as outer direct L-automorphisms, applied to the profinite completion of PSL(2,Z), is essentially the setting in which GT (with λ = 1) and Gal(Q̄/Q^ab) act. The characteristic-ness of Π_{0,3} proved here is what lets such automorphisms restrict to the profinite F_2.
missed.quote: tout automorphisme de la structure de groupe de Γ^+_{0,3} (pas nécessairement un L-auto) conserve le sous-groupe distingué Π_{0,3}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This links Grothendieck's abstract L-group formalism to the known descriptions of Out of the profinite completion of PSL(2,Z) and of the profinite braid group B_3 modulo its centre in GT theory (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura). It is a mild framing point rather than a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: The lemma is classical and elementary. What is new is only the archival detail: the L-group framework, the 'direct Teichmüller group', and a speculative, imprecise characterization conjecture for PSL(2,Z). These are interesting as Grothendieck's alternative to groupes à lacets but contain no substantial unpublished theorem.
transcription_corrections: The target group written '\widehat{\Gamma}_3' is the symmetric group 𝔖_3; Grothendieck's 𝔖 resembles a G.

The hats on Γ^+_{0,3} are likely spurious. The manuscript glyph is Grothendieck's script Γ/𝔖 without a visible hat, and the context (presentation ρ^3 = σ^2 = 1, comparison with Sl(2,Z)/±1) concerns the discrete group.
'tout L-[auto-]aut[?]/de' reads 'tout L-automorphisme direct de' (with 'direct' inserted above the line).
Last line: 'de Γ^+_{0,3} par ρ^3 = σ^2 = 1', with the struck words 'conditions ... homomorphisme surjectif' replaced by 'On utilise la présentation'.
